newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban militia attack north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban militia attack north of Kabul.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia said on Sunday it had launched a successful attack on the forces of a northern alliance on a front near Kabul that has been at stalemate for several weeks.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), based in the western Pakistani city of Peshawar, quoted Taleban sources as saying Taleban fighters had advanced at least five km (three miles) in Saturday night's attack.

It quoted the sources as saying in the southern Afghan city of Kandahar, where the purist Islamic Taleban have their headquarters, as saying at least 24 fighters from both sides were killed or wounded.

The agency quoted the sources as saying Taleban fighters had entered the village of Kalakan, 25 km (19 miles) north of Kabul that had been occupied by the forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
The Taleban captured Kabul on September 27 and then pushed north before being rolled back by a Masood counter-offensive. Masood was then joined by northern Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum.
For the past few weeks, the two sides have been fighting over a band of hills that runs part way across the Shamali valley around Kalakan.
"Heavy fighting is going on in the area and we expect some more advances," AIP quoted one Taleban source as saying.
Attempts by the United Nations and Pakistan to forge a ceasefire that would lead to peace talks to end 17 years of civil war in Afghanistan have so far come to nothing.
